about_me_page_description: I am Petr Závodný, a Shiatsu therapist in Brno. I take a holistic approach – massage, movement, diet and everyday habits. Read about how I work.
about_me_page_heading: Petr Závodný – Shiatsu Therapist in Brno
about_me_page_title: Petr Závodný, Shiatsu Therapist in Brno | Petrklíč
about_me_part1_1: My name is Petr Závodný. I have been practicing Shiatsu massage professionally since 2009. I gained my knowledge through long-term study of Rojin-Liang Shiatsu, Koho Shiatsu, and the Darja Shiatsu School. I continue to develop my skills to this day.
about_me_part1_2: I was introduced to traditional Shiatsu massage in 2006 during my study of the martial art Hakkoryu Jiu-Jitsu, which includes Shiatsu (the founder of Hakkoryu JJ, Ryosuke Okuyama, is also the founder of the Japanese Koho Shiatsu school). I personally experienced the incredible potential of this massage method and decided to explore it more deeply. Over time, this exploration became my profession.
about_me_part1_4: In 2014, I completed a three-year training program called Body, Heart and Soul, organized in our country by Alan Lowen, founder of the Art of Being.
about_me_part1_5: My other interests include yoga, sports, contact improvisation, tantra, and above all, studying the endless possibilities and transformations of life.
about_me_part2_1: My goal is for all my clients to leave satisfied and in a better mood than when they arrived. If you prefer a relaxed body over a stiff one and want to feel good in your body, I am here for you. Nothing compares to the feeling of sudden relief from long-term issues and having blood and energy flow to areas where you used to feel only pain and tension.
about_me_part2_2: People can help others in many ways; my way is to help people using Shiatsu techniques. I approach each client holistically, so I also offer my experience in healthy lifestyle practices (exercise, body awareness, diet, daily habits, thought patterns, interpersonal relationships...) if you're interested.
about_me_part4_1: I have many years of experience, but experience alone does not mean much. More importantly, even after all these years, I still have the same personal drive to offer my clients the highest quality care and to respect their time. This can only be achieved through full presence and attention to both the clients and the technical aspects of my work. I also focus on personal development, which opens doors to deeper levels of perception and understanding of people.
about_me_part4_2: I can empathize with your feelings and needs because I have experienced fatigue, exhaustion, and pain myself. I know what it’s like when someone needs help and someone is able to bring relief.

faq_q1: What happens during a treatment and how long does it take?
faq_a1: The whole treatment takes about 60–75 minutes, of which the bodywork itself is about 40 minutes. You lie on a futon on the floor, wearing comfortable loose clothing. Before the massage we have a short talk to agree on your goals and any health limitations. After the treatment there is time to settle and, if you wish, to talk about what came up during the session.
faq_a2: My philosophy is that a pleasant treatment allows for better work and deeper relaxation of the body. That is why I work sensitively and only as firmly as feels pleasant. If needed, I can use stronger pressure, but only once even that stronger work feels pleasant. In some cases pain cannot be avoided completely – then I will keep talking with you and adjust the intensity so it does not reduce the effect of the treatment.
faq_a3: The treatment is done in clothing. Comfortable, loose clothes you feel good in are best. I want you to feel comfortable and at ease, so how much you wear is largely up to you. The only thing that is not suitable is very tight, non-stretchy clothing, such as tight sports leggings that restrict free movement.
faq_q4: How should I prepare for a treatment?
faq_a4: Come in comfortable clothing, or bring some to change into. Before the treatment it is best to avoid heavy meals, alcohol and other drugs.
faq_q5: How often should I come for Shiatsu?
faq_a5: How often depends on your individual needs. At the beginning I recommend a treatment once every 1–2 weeks; with long-term regular visits, once every 3–5 weeks is enough. After your treatment I can always tell you which frequency suits you.
faq_a6: Shiatsu is possible during pregnancy, but it is important to let me know and tell me how far along you are. I adapt or leave out some techniques to keep the treatment safe and comfortable for both mother and baby. I always recommend consulting your doctor before a treatment during pregnancy.
faq_q7: How much does a Shiatsu treatment cost?
faq_a7: A single treatment costs 1,200 CZK. Prepaid packages are cheaper – for example 4 treatments for 4,000 CZK, which makes one treatment 1,000 CZK.
faq_q8: How do I book a Shiatsu treatment?
faq_a8: You can book by phone at +420 775 915 121, by e-mail at shiatsu@napismi.cz, via the form on the Contact page, or any other way we agree on.
